summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission after allogeneic cord transplant, chronic kidney disease, and systolic heart failure, was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. He was diagnosed with adenovirus gastroenteritis, confirmed by positive stool and blood viral cultures, and treated with a single dose of cidofovir and IVIG, leading to viral clearance. His hospital course was complicated by a recurrent perirectal abscess requiring incision and drainage, multifocal pneumonia that progressed to acute respiratory failure necessitating 6 days of mechanical ventilation, and acute on chronic systolic heart failure with pulmonary edema managed with diuresis. He also developed acute tubular necrosis, likely secondary to cidofovir and volume fluctuations, with creatinine stabilizing by discharge. His macrocytic anemia worsened, with hemoglobin dropping to 7.2 g/dL, but he declined a bone marrow biopsy. HHV-6 levels peaked but resolved without treatment. He was discharged home with services on Lasix, fluconazole, adjusted Bactrim prophylaxis, and a nebulizer, with follow-up planned for lab monitoring and iron chelation evaluation.
problems: Abscess of anal and rectal regions
